# Axis Bank FY25 Annual Report Summary

Axis Bank demonstrated resilient performance in FY25 despite global economic uncertainty, delivering consolidated RoA of 1.77% and RoE of 16.89%. The Bank maintained fortress-like balance sheet strength with net NPA at just 0.33%, ₹11,957 crores in non-NPA provisions, and CET-1 ratio of 14.67% (up 93 bps year-on-year through organic accretion).

**Financial Performance:** High RAROC focus segments—Small Business Banking, SME, and Mid-Corporate—grew 14% year-on-year, now comprising ~23% of the loan book (up ~740 bps over four years). Retail term deposits increased 8%, retail loans grew 7%, and Burgundy Private AUM expanded 16%. Corporate loans rose 8%, mid-corporate book grew 10%, and SME lending increased 14%. Operating subsidiaries delivered combined PAT of ₹1,768 crores (11% growth) with total investment of ₹3,812 crores.

**Strategic Expansion:** Physical infrastructure expanded significantly with 5,879 branches across 3,194 cities (adding 500 branches in FY25), 13,941 ATMs, and 89% district coverage. Digital engagement strengthened with ~3 crore mobile banking customers, 8.7 billion transactions (36% growth), and ₹25.7 trillion mobile banking spends (20% growth). WhatsApp banking reached 30 million users, facilitating ₹191 crores in FD bookings.

**Risk Management:** The Bank maintained industry-leading governance standards, earning top-tier "Leadership" rating in the Indian Corporate Governance Scorecard. However, global headwinds persist—IMF revised global growth forecast downward by 0.5% to 2.8% due to trade tensions and currency volatility.

**ESG Impact:** Axis Bank Foundation surpassed 'Mission 2 Million,' impacting ~2.05 million participants across 300 districts nationwide by March 2025.

# Axis Bank FY25 Annual Report Summary

## Key Financial Metrics

Axis Bank issued ₹3,925 crores in non-convertible debentures (Series-8) in September 2024 at 7.45% coupon rate, maturing in 2034, to fund infrastructure and affordable housing. The Bank redeemed ₹5,705 crores of senior unsecured debentures in December 2024 and ₹850 crores of Basel III Tier 2 bonds in February 2025. The Bank has approval to raise up to ₹35,000 crores through debt securities on private placement basis.

## Accounting Policy Changes

From April 1, 2024, the Bank adopted RBI's revised investment framework, resulting in significant balance sheet impacts. The Investment Reserve Account balance of ₹242.29 crores was transferred to general reserves, along with ₹1,217.86 crores (net of tax) from reversal of depreciation provisions, increasing net worth. Under the new framework, AFS investments showed net appreciation of ₹110.39 crores (net of tax) in AFS Reserve, while FVTPL securities generated net gains of ₹700.51 crores in FY25.

## Risk Management Framework

The Bank employs comprehensive market risk management using Value at Risk (VaR) calculated via historical simulation at 99% confidence level over one-day holding periods with 250-day horizons. Risk management encompasses discriminatory power assessment, stress testing, back testing, and scenario analysis, supplemented by position limits and marked-to-market evaluations. Liquidity risk is managed through Asset Liability Management policies, maintaining Liquidity Coverage Ratio per RBI guidelines. Operational risk management covers core processes, change management, outsourcing, continuity, and information security through defined governance structures and monitoring systems.

# Axis Bank FY25 Financial Performance Summary

## Key Financial Metrics

Axis Bank reported consolidated net profit of ₹28,055 crores in FY25, growing 6% year-on-year. Standalone net profit reached ₹26,373 crores (up 6% from ₹24,861 crores), with operating profit rising 13% to ₹42,105 crores. Operating revenue increased 10% to ₹79,605 crores, driven by 9% growth in Net Interest Income (NII) to ₹54,348 crores and 13% growth in non-interest income to ₹25,257 crores. However, profitability metrics declined significantly—EPS dropped from ₹80.67 to ₹71.37 (excluding exceptional items), ROE fell from 18.86% to 16.52%, and ROA decreased from 1.83% to 1.74%.

Balance sheet expanded with total assets reaching ₹16,09,930 crores (9% growth). Advances grew 8% to ₹10,40,811 crores, while deposits increased 10% to ₹11,72,952 crores. Retail advances comprised 60% of the loan book, growing 7%, while wholesale advances rose 9%.

## Risk Factors

Asset quality deteriorated noticeably. Gross NPA ratio increased from 2.82% to 3.70%, and Net NPA rose from 0.73% to 1.05%. Provisions surged 91% to ₹7,759 crores, primarily due to higher slippages and interest reversals. Provision Coverage Ratio declined from 75% to 72%. Net Interest Margin compressed 9 basis points to 3.98% as cost of funds increased 21 bps to 5.46%, outpacing the 7 bps yield improvement. CASA ratio declined 328 bps to 39.26%.

## Strategic Highlights

The bank maintained robust capitalization with Capital Adequacy Ratio at 19.12% and Tier 1 at 16.47%. Domestic subsidiaries delivered strong performance with 46% ROI and contributed 37 bps to consolidated ROE. Cost-to-asset ratio improved to 1.96%. Management projects medium-term system credit growth in low-to-mid teens, supported by 7%+ potential GDP growth and recovering private capex.

# Axis Bank FY25 Annual Report Summary

Axis Bank's second Integrated Annual Report for FY25 demonstrates strong governance frameworks and comprehensive risk management. The Board comprises **13 Directors**, including **8 Independent Directors** and **2 Women Directors**, with **85% possessing finance expertise** and **69% having banking experience**. The governance structure operates through multiple specialized committees, including Risk Management, Audit, IT & Digital Strategy, and a pioneering ESG Committee established in 2021.

The Bank received **673 whistleblower complaints** during the fiscal year, with **54 sexual harassment cases** filed and **50 disposed of**. The vigilance function processed **343 cases**, resulting in disciplinary action against **427 officials**, reinforcing the Bank's zero-tolerance approach to misconduct. **33 workshops** were conducted on sexual harassment awareness.

Risk management remains central to operations, overseen by the Risk Management Committee and supported by the independent Risk Management Department. The Bank has strengthened cyber security controls through the Information System Security Committee, implementing multifactor authentication, real-time fraud monitoring, and advanced threat intelligence. The Financial Crime Intelligence unit employs cutting-edge technology and analytics to create a fraud-resistant environment.

The report, prepared according to the International Integrated Reporting Framework and SEBI guidelines, received independent audit assurance from M/s. M M Nissim & Co LLP and M/s. KKC & Associates LLP, while SGS India provided reasonable assurance for BRSR Core disclosures. Subsidiary governance is ensured through the Subsidiary Governance Committee, aligning practices across the financial conglomerate while maintaining regulatory compliance and transparency.

# Axis Bank FY25 Annual Report Summary

## Financial Performance and Strategic Targets

Axis Bank exceeded its sustainable wholesale lending target of ₹30,000 crores well ahead of the 2026 deadline, achieving ₹30,409 crores by March 2024. The Bank subsequently raised this target to ₹60,000 crores by 2030, reaching ₹48,412 crores by March 2025. In retail segments, the Bank achieved 7.14% electric vehicle penetration in two-wheeler loans and 2.92% in four-wheeler loans, progressing toward the 6% and 4% fiscal 2027 targets respectively. India's GDP growth is estimated at 6.5% for fiscal 2026, with the banking sector benefiting from rural demand, infrastructure investment, and financial formalization.

## Risk Management and Governance

The Bank maintained exposure to coal and thermal power within glide path limits across fiscal 2023-2025, demonstrating commitment to scaling down carbon-intensive sectors. A standalone Board-level ESG Committee, India's first among banks established in 2021, met four times in fiscal 2025 to oversee ESG initiatives. Risk management frameworks now incorporate climate stress testing, scenario analysis, and expanded environmental and social risk assessments across the portfolio.

## Strategic Initiatives

Under "Bharat Banking," the Bank focuses on rural and semi-urban financial inclusion through digital innovations and strategic alliances. Women's representation in the workforce reached 27.7% by March 2025, progressing toward the 30% target by fiscal 2027. The Bank surpassed its Mission 2 Million tree plantation goal, planting 3.27 million trees and upgrading the target to 8 million trees by 2030, demonstrating commitment to climate action aligned with UN SDGs and India's Paris Agreement commitments.

# HDFC Bank FY25 Annual Report Summary

HDFC Bank's FY 2024-25 Integrated Annual Report demonstrates strong financial performance nearly two years post-merger, with total income reaching ₹3,46,149.3 crore and profit after tax of ₹67,347.4 crore. The bank maintained healthy metrics including Return on Average Assets at 1.91%, Return on Equity at 14.6%, and a robust Capital Adequacy Ratio of 19.6%. Asset quality remained strong with Net NPA at just 0.43%, while the cost-to-income ratio stood at 40.5%. The bank proposed a dividend of ₹22.0 per share.

The bank serves 9.7 crore customers through an extensive network of 24,854 banking outlets, including 9,455 branches (51% in semi-urban and rural areas), 21,139 ATMs, and 15,399 business correspondents across 4,150 cities. Digital transformation progressed significantly, with 97% of financial transactions and 86% of acquisitions now digital, achieving 99.95% customer uptime.

Strategic priorities focus on "Employee First, Customer First, Technology First, and Power of the Group." The workforce of 2,14,521 employees (26.14% women) received 1.25 crore learning hours, though attrition remained at 22.60%.

Risk management encompasses ten key areas: credit, market, compliance, operational, climate, liquidity, reputation, technology, cyber/data, and subsidiary spillover risks. The bank achieved zero environmental and social non-compliance incidents.

Sustainability efforts include ₹1,068.03 crore CSR spending through Parivartan, impacting 10.56 crore lives cumulatively. The bank operates 2,507 green-certified branches, achieved 45% reduction in Scope 1&2 emission intensity, and maintains an 18.69% sustainable finance portfolio, earning MSCI AA ESG rating.

# HDFC Bank FY25 Annual Report Summary: ESOP Schemes and Executive Compensation

## Employee Stock Option Plans (ESOP)

HDFC Bank operated extensive stock-based compensation programs during FY25, with multiple ESOP schemes (Plan F, G, H) and Restricted Stock Unit (RSU) schemes approved between 2013-2024. As of March 31, 2025, **15.63 crore options/units remained in force** across all schemes.

During FY25, **55.31 lakh options were exercised**, generating total proceeds of **₹74,321.63 crore** (comprising ₹5.53 crore share capital, ₹63,409.66 crore share premium, and ₹10,856.66 crore perquisite tax). The weighted average exercise price was ₹1,198.42 for ESOPs and ₹1 for RSUs.

Key new grants included **22.16 lakh options under Plan H-ESOS 58** and **4.17 lakh under ESOS 59** at grant prices of ₹1,734.20 and ₹1,677.30 respectively. RSU schemes granted **60.42 lakh units (RSU 009)** at face value of ₹1. Options typically vest over 2-4 years and must be exercised within specified periods.

## Executive Compensation (FY25)

**Managing Director Sashidhar Jagdishan** received total compensation of ₹12.06 crore, including ₹4.67 crore performance bonus and **2.12 lakh stock options** for FY24 performance. Other Executive Directors: **Kaizad Bharucha** (₹13.01 crore with 1.30 lakh options), **Bhavesh Zaveri** (₹6.52 crore with 78,602 options), and **V. Srinivasa Rangan** (₹10.90 crore with 6.03 lakh options, including one-time grants).

## Valuation Methodology

Fair value calculations used the Black-Scholes model with risk-free rates of 6.73%-7.19%, expected volatility of 20.05%-27.70%, and expected life of 1-8 years.

# HDFC Bank FY25 Summary

HDFC Bank completed its first full year post-merger with HDFC Limited, demonstrating resilient performance despite global headwinds. Net profit grew 10.7% to ₹67,347.4 crore, while Net Interest Income increased 13.0% to ₹1,22,670.1 crore. The balance sheet expanded 8% to ₹39,10,199 crore, with advances at ₹26,19,609 crore and deposits reaching ₹27,14,715 crore—deposits growing 2.5 times faster than loans at 14.1%.

The Bank strategically repositioned its balance sheet, reducing the credit-deposit ratio from 110% at merger to 96%, and lowering high-cost borrowings to 14%. Asset quality remained pristine with Gross NPAs at just 1.33%, Return on Average Assets at 1.91%, and Capital Adequacy Ratio at 19.6%. NIM stood at 3.48%.

The merger created India's leading financial conglomerate, adding home loans and subsidiaries including HDFC Life, HDFC ERGO, and HDFC AMC, enabling comprehensive cross-selling opportunities. The Bank captured 14.6% incremental deposit market share with only 5% branch market share, demonstrating exceptional franchise strength.

Strategic priorities include achieving carbon neutrality by FY32, with renewable energy constituting 3.22% of electricity mix (up from 0.39%). Digital transformation accelerated with 97% of transactions through digital channels and 99% personal loans originated digitally. The Bank invested ₹1,068 crore in CSR, impacting 10+ crore lives across six focus areas.

Key risks include global tariff uncertainties, geopolitical tensions affecting trade flows, and domestic consumption volatility. However, management expressed confidence in growing advances on par with the system in FY26 and exceeding it in FY27, supported by strengthened balance sheet fundamentals and technological investments in GenAI and cybersecurity.

# HDFC Bank FY25 Annual Report Summary

## Financial Performance

HDFC Bank demonstrated resilient performance in FY25 despite challenging liquidity conditions. Profit After Tax grew 10.7% to ₹67,347.4 crore, while Net Interest Margin maintained stability at 3.48%. The Bank strategically recalibrated its balance sheet, achieving deposit growth of 14.1% while tempering advances growth to 5.4% to improve the loan-to-deposit ratio. Asset quality remained robust with Gross Non-Performing Assets at just 1.33%. The Board recommended a dividend of ₹22.0 per equity share, subject to shareholder approval.

## Risk Management and Regulatory Environment

Operating as a Domestic Systemically Important Bank (D-SIB), the Bank faced enhanced regulatory expectations in the post-merger environment following HDFC Limited's amalgamation effective July 1, 2023. Management undertook significant transformation of the compliance function, reinforcing governance, transparency, and regulatory excellence. Internal systems were recalibrated to ensure full statutory adherence, with continued technology investments for accuracy and timeliness in reporting.

## Strategic Direction

The Bank's strategy was shaped by constrained system-wide credit growth due to restricted liquidity, prompting a deliberate focus on increasing deposits in the funding mix. Leadership emphasized maintaining the institution's four-decade legacy of values while navigating growth. The roadmap prioritizes sustainable balance sheet management, customer service improvements, and leveraging the expanded distribution network gained through the HDFC merger. The governance structure includes 53.85% independent directors and three women directors, ensuring robust oversight across multiple specialized board committees covering risk, audit, IT strategy, and ESG initiatives.

# HDFC Bank FY25 Annual Report Summary

HDFC Bank delivered strong financial performance in FY25 despite integration challenges from the HDFC Limited merger (effective July 1, 2023). Net profit grew 10.7% to ₹67,347 crore, with earnings per share rising to ₹88.3. The balance sheet expanded 8.1% to ₹39.10 lakh crore, driven by deposits growing 14.1% to ₹27.15 lakh crore and advances increasing 5.4% to ₹26.20 lakh crore.

**Key Financial Metrics:** Return on Equity declined to 14.6% from 16.1%, while Return on Assets fell to 1.91% from 1.98%. Net Interest Margin stood at 3.48%, with cost-to-income ratio marginally increasing to 40.5%. The bank maintained a strong Capital Adequacy Ratio of 19.6% (Tier 1: 17.7%), significantly above the regulatory minimum of 11.7%. A dividend of ₹22 per share was proposed, reflecting a 25% payout ratio.

**Asset Quality:** Gross NPA ratio increased modestly to 1.33% from 1.24%, remaining among the industry's lowest. Net NPA ratio was 0.43%, with coverage ratio at 172.1% including general and floating provisions. Total provisions declined to ₹11,649 crore from ₹23,492 crore, primarily due to previous year's ₹10,900 crore floating provision.

**Strategic Highlights:** The bank employed 2.15 lakh staff across India, with strong regional presence. CASA deposits comprised 34.8% of total deposits. Revenue composition showed 68.9% from advances interest and 16.6% from investments. The bank maintained all AAA ratings across instruments and continued treasury operations generating ₹4,919 crore from forex/derivative transactions, while expanding digital and embedded banking capabilities.

# ICICI Bank FY25 Annual Report Summary

## Financial Performance

ICICI Bank delivered strong results in FY25 with profit after tax increasing 15.5% to ₹472.27 billion from ₹408.88 billion in FY24. Net interest income grew 9.2% to ₹811.65 billion, driven by 14.5% growth in average interest-earning assets, though partially offset by net interest margin compression of 21 basis points to 4.32%. Fee income expanded 14.8% to ₹238.70 billion, while dividend from subsidiaries rose 26.3% to ₹26.19 billion. Operating expenses increased 8.3% to ₹423.72 billion, with cost-to-income ratio improving to 38.63% from 40.23%.

## Balance Sheet Growth

Total assets grew 13.2% to ₹21,182.40 billion, with advances rising 13.3% to ₹13,417.66 billion (domestic advances up 13.9%). Deposits increased 14.0% to ₹16,103.48 billion, though CASA ratio moderated to 39.0% from 40.4%. Net worth expanded 22.5% to ₹2,920.77 billion. The bank maintained strong capital adequacy with total CAR at 16.55%, Tier-1 at 15.94%, and CET-1 at 15.94%, all above regulatory requirements.

## Risk Factors

Provisions increased significantly by 28.5% to ₹46.83 billion, primarily due to higher NPA additions in retail and rural segments. Provision coverage ratio declined to 76.2% from 80.3%. The cost of funds rose 24 basis points to 5.10%, driven by 43 basis points increase in domestic term deposit costs to 6.65%. Interest spread compressed by 26 basis points to 3.59%.

## Strategic Highlights

The bank expanded its network to 6,983 branches and 16,285 ATMs/CRMs. CSR spending totaled ₹8,011.2 million. With 53.5% of domestic loans linked to external benchmarks, the bank remains sensitive to rate movements and RBI's 50 basis point repo rate cut from February-April 2025.

# ICICI Bank FY25 Annual Report Summary

## Key Financial Metrics

ICICI Bank delivered strong standalone performance in FY2025. Net profit rose 15.5% to ₹472.27 billion from ₹408.88 billion in FY2024. Profit before tax (excluding treasury income) increased 11.4% to ₹607.13 billion. Net interest income grew to ₹621.29 billion with net interest margin at 4.32%. Core operating profit jumped 12.5% to ₹653.96 billion, while operating expenses rose 8.3% to ₹423.72 billion. 

Consolidated profit after tax reached ₹510.29 billion, up 15.3%, with consolidated profit before tax at ₹730.04 billion. The Board recommended a dividend of ₹11.00 per equity share.

Total assets expanded 13.2% to ₹21,182.40 billion, with net advances growing 13.3% to ₹13,417.66 billion (domestic advances up 13.9%). Deposits increased to ₹16,103.48 billion. Investment portfolio stood at ₹5,047.57 billion, including ₹3,996.86 billion in government securities.

## Asset Quality

Asset quality showed significant improvement. Gross NPAs declined to ₹241.66 billion with gross NPA ratio improving to 0.4% (from 0.4% in FY2024, based on customer assets). Net NPA ratio remained stable at 0.4%. Provision coverage strengthened with general provisions for standard assets at ₹64.45 billion and contingency provisions at ₹131 billion.

The corporate portfolio maintained healthy credit quality with 74.8% rated A- and above. Rural advances reached ₹783.40 billion. Priority sector lending averaged 18.0% of adjusted net bank credit, meeting regulatory targets.

## Strategic Developments

On March 24, 2025, ICICI Securities became a wholly-owned subsidiary following delisting, with 56 million equity shares issued to shareholders under the Scheme of Arrangement. The Bank allotted 43.6 million shares under employee stock option schemes during the year.

Capital adequacy remained robust with consolidated Tier-1 CAR at 15.81% (requirement: 9.70%) and total CAR at 16.41% (requirement: 11.70%). The Bank maintained consistent dividend history while appropriating ₹118.07 billion to statutory reserves.

## Risk Factors

The report identifies key risks including statutory and regulatory changes, international economic conditions, political instability, increase in non-performing loans, interest rate and foreign exchange fluctuations, sovereign rating changes, and market risks. CSR spending of ₹2,740 million was transferred to Unspent CSR Account for ongoing projects, with ₹879.8 million remaining from FY2024.

# ICICI Bank FY25 Annual Report Summary

## Subsidiary and Associate Structure

ICICI Bank maintains 100% ownership in 13 wholly-owned subsidiaries including ICICI Bank UK, ICICI Bank Canada, ICICI Securities Limited, and ICICI Home Finance. The bank holds majority stakes in key listed entities: ICICI Lombard General Insurance (51.55%), ICICI Prudential Life Insurance (51.03%), and ICICI Prudential Asset Management (51.00%). Associate holdings include India Infradebt Limited (42.33%) and Falcon Tyres Limited (26.39%). On June 27, 2025, the Board approved purchasing up to 2% additional shareholding in ICICI Prudential AMC to maintain majority control.

## Major Corporate Action

A significant milestone was the merger of ICICI Securities with the Bank, effective March 24, 2025. The scheme resulted in ICICI Securities becoming a wholly-owned subsidiary after delisting from stock exchanges. The Bank allotted 56,008,117 equity shares on March 26, 2025, to public shareholders at an approved swap ratio, including 51,723 shares for fractional entitlements.

## Shareholding and Capital Structure

Total equity shares outstanding reached 7,121,927,830, with 99.86% in demat form. Foreign institutional investors hold the largest stake at 37.30%, followed by mutual funds (24.31%) and ADS holders via Deutsche Bank Trust (18.60%). Insurance companies hold 9.16%. Individual shareholders account for 6.39% of total shareholding. The bank has 662.40 million ADSs outstanding, equivalent to 1,324.80 million equity shares.

## Employee Stock Programs

Under the Employees Stock Option Scheme 2000, the Bank has granted 639.49 million options (8.98% of issued capital), with 169,866,927 options outstanding at year-end. During FY25, 42,832,398 options were exercised, generating ₹14,374 million. The newer Employees Stock Unit Scheme 2022 had 8,032,295 units outstanding, with weighted average fair value of units granted at ₹1,120.43.

# ICICI Bank FY25 Annual Report Summary

## Key Financial Metrics

ICICI Bank delivered robust financial performance in FY25, with profit after tax reaching ₹472.27 billion (up 15.5% YoY) and profit before tax excluding treasury at ₹607.13 billion (up 11.4% YoY). Consolidated profit after tax stood at ₹510.29 billion. The bank maintained a strong net interest margin of 4.32% with total assets reaching ₹21,182.40 billion. Loans and advances grew to ₹13,417.66 billion while total deposits stood at ₹16,103.48 billion. Capital adequacy ratio remained healthy at 16.55% with Common Equity Tier 1 ratio at 15.94%. Consolidated return on equity was 18.0%. The bank demonstrated improved asset quality with net NPA ratio declining from 0.42% to 0.39% during the year.

## Strategic Highlights

The bank expanded its physical footprint to nearly 7,000 business centres (460 added during FY25) while strengthening digital capabilities. The Business Banking portfolio serving businesses with turnover up to ₹7.50 billion grew 33.7% to ₹2,633.67 billion, contributing 19.6% of net advances. Key digital innovations included launching DigiEase for seamless business banking onboarding, iCRM platform for 360° customer relationship management, and SmartLock security feature. The bank's iMobile app processed 558 million transactions worth ₹11,238 billion, while InstaBIZ transactions grew 37%. CASA deposits showed healthy growth with current accounts up 11.7% and savings accounts up 10.2%. Active credit cards reached 18 million.

## Risk Factors and Sustainability

The bank maintained disciplined risk management with 74.8% of corporate loans rated A- and above. It emphasized "Return of Capital" through quality counterparty selection and agile risk management across credit, market, liquidity, operational, legal, cyber, and compliance areas. On sustainability, the bank set a carbon neutrality target for Scope 1 and 2 emissions by FY32, with 5 million square feet of premises IGBC-certified. The sustainable finance portfolio reached ₹906 billion (34.2% in green financing). CSR allocation increased to ₹8.01 billion, with major initiatives including an ₹18.00 billion commitment for three greenfield cancer care facilities. The bank planted 1.2 million saplings during FY25 and achieved 38% renewable energy usage.

Human capital initiatives included deepening share-linked compensation to 20,700 employees with women comprising 32% of workforce (42,000 employees).

# ICICI Bank FY25 Annual Report Summary

## Governance Structure

ICICI Bank maintains a robust governance framework with Sandeep Bakhshi as Managing Director & CEO and Pradeep Kumar Sinha as Non-Executive Part-time Chairman (effective July 1, 2024). The Board comprises multiple Independent Directors overseeing specialized committees including Audit, Risk, Credit, IT Strategy, and Corporate Social Responsibility.

## Key Personnel Changes

Significant leadership transitions occurred during FY25. Girish Chandra Chaturvedi retired as Independent Director and Chairperson on June 30, 2024. Rohit Bhasin and Punit Sood joined as Independent Directors for five-year terms beginning July 26, 2024, and October 1, 2024, respectively. Rakesh Jha and Sandeep Batra received RBI approval for re-appointment as Executive Directors in June 2025.

## Risk Management Framework

The Bank identifies eight principal risk categories: credit, market, liquidity, operational, technology, cyber, compliance, and reputational risks. Management operates under a "risk-calibrated growth" strategy targeting profit before tax excluding treasury. The Risk Management Group, headed by the Chief Risk Officer reporting to the Board's Risk Committee, maintains independence from business operations. The Bank implements Enterprise Risk Management and Risk Appetite Frameworks with four-year capital planning through Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP).

## Corporate Actions

The merger of ICICI Securities became effective March 24, 2025, following National Company Law Tribunal approvals in August and October 2024. ICICI Securities was delisted from stock exchanges, with the Bank previously holding 74.73% equity. The Bank raised ₹30,000 million through senior unsecured bonds during FY25.

## Compliance and Controls

Statutory auditors B S R & Co. LLP and C N K & Associates LLP submitted unqualified audit reports. The Bank received 117 sexual harassment complaints under the POSH Act, all resolved within 90 days. No significant regulatory orders impacting going concern status were reported.

# Kotak Mahindra Bank FY25 Annual Report Summary

**Financial Performance:**
Kotak Mahindra Bank demonstrated solid growth in FY25 with customer base expanding 6% year-over-year and customer assets (including advances, IBPC, BRDS and credit substitutes) growing 13% YoY. The Group's CSR expenditure reached ₹389.3 crore, benefiting over 14.6 lakh people. Priority Sector Lending (PSL) compliance showed strong performance with 13.89% allocation to non-corporate farmers, 8.96% to micro-enterprises, and 14.36% to weaker sections.

**Strategic Initiatives:**
The bank strengthened its ESG framework through Board-approved policies on green and sustainable finance, with oversight from the CSR and ESG Committee. Key achievements included ISO/IEC 27001 certification for Information Security Management, ISO 45001:2018 certification covering 20% of workforce across 8 offices, and 16 LEED/IGBC certified premises. Green finance commitments totaled ₹999 crore for LEED-certified buildings, ₹225 crore for renewable energy projects, and over ₹1,000 crore for water infrastructure and waste management.

**Risk Management & Sustainability:**
The bank enhanced ESG risk evaluation through a revamped ESG Management Systems Plan and conducted transition risk assessments for Power and Cement sectors. Renewable electricity usage reached 5.5%. Social finance initiatives included supporting ~23 lakh active microcredit women borrowers, with 100% women representation in BSS and Sonata lending portfolios.

**Workforce Metrics:**
Women represented 26.4% of Group workforce (26.0% at Bank level), with 8.5% in senior management. Training investments increased 29% YoY, averaging 49.5 hours per employee. Female employee turnover decreased 19% YoY, indicating improved retention.

# Kotak Mahindra Bank FY25 Annual Report Summary

**Key Financial Metrics:**
Kotak Mahindra Bank demonstrated strong financial stability in FY25. The Group maintained a Capital Adequacy Ratio of 23.30% and Liquidity Coverage Ratio of 135.46%, well above regulatory requirements. Net Stable Funding Ratio stood at 115.71%. Total Loans and Advances (net) reached ₹426,909.20 crores, with Net NPA ratio at a low 0.31%. NPA provisions totaled ₹4,790.41 crores. The bank maintained AAA credit ratings as of March 31, 2025.

**Governance Structure:**
The Board comprises 55% independent directors with 27% gender diversity. The leadership team averages approximately 20 years tenure with the Group. The bank maintains ISO/IEC 27001 certification for information security management and operates under a robust Three Lines of Defence risk management model.

**Risk Management Framework:**
The Enterprise-wide Risk Management framework addresses seven key financial risks: credit, liquidity, interest rate, market, fraud, operational, and group risk. A dedicated 24×7 Security Operations Centre monitors cybersecurity threats. Following RBI's April 24, 2024 order restricting onboarding of new digital customers and credit card issuance due to IT examination deficiencies, the bank implemented comprehensive gap assessments, upgraded policies, established the IT Risk and Information Security Committee (IRISC), and deployed Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR) solutions.

**Strategic Initiatives:**
The bank enhanced fraud risk management through automated workflows and background verification systems. All employees receive anti-corruption training covering AML standards and KYC norms. The bank operates comprehensive whistleblower mechanisms and maintains zero reported legal actions related to anti-competitive behavior in FY25.

# Kotak Mahindra Bank FY25 Summary

Kotak Mahindra Bank demonstrated robust growth in FY25, with consolidated total assets reaching ₹8.8 trillion (16% 4-year CAGR) and market capitalization of ₹4.3 trillion as of March 31, 2025. The Group serves 5.3 crore customers through 5,378 branches across India, supported by 114,000+ employees.

**Financial Performance:** Net profit surged to ₹22,126 crore (22% 4-year CAGR), significantly boosted by a ₹3,013 crore gain from divesting its 70% stake in Kotak Mahindra General Insurance to Zurich Insurance for ₹4,095.82 crore. Operating profit reached ₹29,045 crore, while net interest income grew to ₹37,394 crore (17% CAGR). Bank advances expanded to ₹319,861 crore (18% CAGR) with deposits at ₹494,707 crore. Asset quality improved with Net NPA declining to 0.31% from 1.21% in FY21. The bank maintained strong capital adequacy at 22.3% (Tier I: 21.1%).

**Business Segments:** Asset Management Company grew AAUM by 35% YoY to ₹468,820 crore, achieving 7.09% market share. Investment Banking maintained #1 ranking in India's ECM for three consecutive years, executing 31 ECM transactions including 18 IPOs. # SBI FY25 Annual Report Summary

**Credit Ratings and Financial Position**

SBI maintains strong credit ratings across agencies: Moody's rated the bank at Baa3/Stable/P-3, S&P at BBB-/Positive/A-3, and Fitch at BBB-/Stable/F3. Domestic instruments received top ratings with AT-1 Bonds, Long Term Bonds, and Tier II Bonds rated AAA/Stable by CRISIL, ICRA, CARE, and India Ratings. As a Domestic Systemically Important Bank (D-SIB), SBI must maintain additional Common Equity Tier 1 capital of 0.80% of risk-weighted assets from April 2025, increased from 0.60%.

**Asset Quality and Recovery**

The bank referred 1,208 cases to NCLT under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, with 983 admitted, 272 resolution plans approved, and 524 liquidation orders issued. Recovery efforts utilize multiple channels including NARCL/ARC sales, SARFAESI Act provisions, DRT filings, and the Rinn Samadhan scheme for small-ticket loans. NPA levels have decreased significantly through these structured recovery mechanisms.

**Risk Management Framework**

SBI employs comprehensive risk management covering credit, market, liquidity, and operational risks. The bank monitors 37 identified industries representing 65% of total advances (excluding retail and agriculture). Credit risk assessment includes ESG Rating Models for large borrowers and Risk-Adjusted Return on Capital (RAROC) framework for exposures above ₹5 crore. Stress tests are conducted bi-annually on credit portfolios, with daily Value-at-Risk monitoring complemented by stressed VaR calculations.

**Treasury and Derivatives Operations**

The bank offers comprehensive derivative products including Rupee Interest Rate Swaps, Foreign Currency Interest Rate Swaps, Cross Currency Swaps, and USD/INR options. From November 2024, Non-Deliverable Options became available to eligible corporates. All transactions follow the Derivatives Policy with defined risk limits including Greeks and PV01 parameters, governed by ISDA agreements and Credit Support Agreements.

**Governance and Compliance**

The Internal Audit Department completed Risk Focused Internal Audit for 14,151 domestic branches in FY2025. The bank maintains 97,81,822 unclaimed shares for 31,439 shareholders in suspense accounts. SBI remains fully compliant with Basel III Capital Regulations and maintains the required 4% leverage ratio under D-SIB requirements.
